requirement.title: Allow generating a formatter for a type declared in a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A project can source-generate IMessagePackFormatter<T> for a type from a referenced assembly that has no MessagePack dependency.
functional: A [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T> gets a generated implementation
Invalid usages produce analyzer diagnostics with documentation
requirement.issueBody:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

agent.summary: Added [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] (Annotations) so a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T> gets a generated implementation for a type without MessagePack attributes. The generator collects T in map mode via a new TypeCollector entry point, emits the existing formatter template as a nested class inside the user's partial class, and emits delegating Serialize/Deserialize members. New analyzer MsgPack019 (with docs, release notes, index entry, README section) flags non-partial classes or classes without exactly one IMessagePackFormatter<T> for a class/struct T. 3 new tests pass; the existing suite was not run.

decisions.decision: Serialize the target type in forced map mode using public instance members only
decisions.why: The referenced type has no [MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes so a keying scheme is needed; map mode needs no attributes and matches [MessagePackObject(true)]
decisions.alternatives: Honor DataMember attributes, or user-defined copies of MessagePack attributes (issue alternatives 1 and 2); int-key array mode

decisions.decision: Emit the normal formatter template as a nested class 'GeneratedImplementation' in the user's partial class, with generated delegating Serialize/Deserialize members
decisions.why: Reuses the existing T4 templates without editing .tt/.cs files that cannot be regenerated here
decisions.alternatives: Edit the templates to emit members directly into the user's class

decisions.decision: Generated user formatters are not added to the generated resolver
decisions.why: The user declares and registers their own formatter instance; adding it would risk duplicate or colliding registrations
decisions.alternatives: Include in resolver via the existing known-formatter mechanism
decisions.evidence: MessagePackGenerator.cs userFormatterSources pipeline is separate from resolver source

decisions.decision: Added analyzer MsgPack019 (Error) for invalid usages
decisions.why: Requirement asks for diagnostics with documentation for invalid usages
decisions.alternatives: Separate IDs for not-partial vs wrong-interface-count
